Seen building DX-merge-queue: ddflow_queue plus a merge argument measured 101,657 bytes; getting back under needed trimming the pins, merge and relation/check_only descriptions, leaving 99,980. Parallel agents adding tools will each hit this. Options: serve rarely used tools only in the all tier and budget the compact core/standard lists separately; or shrink the shared descriptions once; or have the budget count per tier. Per-tier budgets match what a session pays for.

FOLDED IN from DX-tool-budget-headroom (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): The MCP tools/list byte budget has almost no headroom; every new parameter trips it
Adding two boolean --queue params (DX-no-hold-and-wait) pushed tools/list to 100427 bytes of the 100000 budget and failed test_mcp_tool_budget, test_mcp_tool_tiers and test_upgrade_dry_run; I had to trim help text to a few words. Wanted: a tool-budget report showing which tools cost most, or per-tier budgets, so authors are not forced to degrade descriptions.

A review's findings print only in the output of the running 'ddflow review' (lost if stdout is not kept); gate status shows counts and 'review triage' needs a finding number, so to read finding N an agent digs chunk_findings out of its event-log line. Add 'ddflow review findings <id> --gate G' listing numbered findings with severity, location, detail and triage state.

FOLDED IN from DX-review-triage-list-findings (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): review triage lists no findings
Triage with no --finding only says 'say which'; the numbered findings (a 5th one included) were visible only via show --json evidence. Make triage list findings with number, location, verdict.

The unit_tests gate runner times out on the full suite (about 7 minutes, longer under load), so agents ran the suite themselves and recorded unit_tests by hand; the ci gate also blocks a shell for 10-20 minutes. Run a gate command as a detached ddflow job (the job engine exists: ddflow job run) with its log path, renew the lease while it runs, record the gate outcome from the exit code when it finishes, and report in status/brief that it is in flight; --wait attaches to it. Regression test: a gate command that sleeps beyond the old timeout is recorded passed when it exits 0, with its log kept.

Filed 2026-10-15 from use (D-file-ddflow-defects). CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-company-workflows): every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

FOLDED IN from DX-gate-timeout-false-fail (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): A gate run that outlives the tool timeout is recorded failed
Found by fleet-pins. A gate run that outlives the calling tool's timeout leaves the gate recorded failed until it is re-run, so a slow ci or unit_tests costs a redundant cycle. Wanted: gate run detaches and records the real outcome when it ends, or marks the gate running meanwhile (see DX-gate-run-detach).

The unit_tests gate runner times out on the full suite (about 7 minutes, longer under load), so agents ran the suite themselves and recorded unit_tests by hand; the ci gate also blocks a shell for 10-20 minutes. Run a gate command as a detached ddflow job (the job engine exists: ddflow job run) with its log path, renew the lease while it runs, record the gate outcome from the exit code when it finishes, and report in status/brief that it is in flight; --wait attaches to it. Regression test: a gate command that sleeps beyond the old timeout is recorded passed when it exits 0, with its log kept.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-company-workflows): every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

FOLDED IN from DX-gate-background-limit (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): Gate runs over MCP hit a 30 minute background limit regardless of gate timeout_s
Bug Bec9936dc6b second half: unit_tests under load exceeded the 30m background limit. The command/timeout are already configurable ([gate.unit_tests].command/timeout_s); the fixed 30m cap of the background runner is not. Make the cap a config knob or have the gate survive it.

Seen building DX-merge-queue: README's MCP tool table (test_readme_tool_table) had no [[pin]] recipe (added readme-tool-table in this change). tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py embeds the CLI command list in an EXPECTED usage line that a new command changes and no recipe re-records; test_readme_catchup needs a prose line per command. The merge queue regenerates only what pins.toml names, so these stay hand-merged. Give the transcript an out-of-line pin file with an update switch and a recipe, and generate or relax the catch-up check.

FOLDED IN from DX-pins-loop-transcript (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): pins regenerate cannot re-record tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py (inline Python literals)
The setup-ops transcript is JSON and re-records per command; the loop transcript keeps its expected output as source literals, so no recipe can rewrite only the differing entries. Move it to a JSON file like the setup-ops one, then add a [[pin]] recipe in .ddflow/pins.toml.

Claiming my own lapsed item needed three different commands (claim, recover --item, claim --force) and the second step is only an instruction text. When the expired lease belongs to the same agent identity, claim should renew it without --force; for another agent's, print the one-line recover-and-force sequence.

Filed 2026-10-15 from use (D-file-ddflow-defects). CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-company-workflows): every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

FOLDED IN from DX-self-wait-wording (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): The claim refusal says 'T1 is waiting for T1' when an item queues behind itself
Found by fleet-nohold. The recorded wait reads 'Recorded: T1 is waiting for T1 (u5pin).' A self-wait is a bug or a mislabeled same-agent re-claim; either report 'already leased to you' or name the real holder. Add a test.

Extend the Forge base of infra/forge.py (it shells out to gh and glab and holds no token) with adapters over tea or the REST API, az devops and the Bitbucket API for PR state, merge and the published ddflow/gates check (B-gap-checks-publish); recorded fixtures per adapter; a missing CLI or login is unavailable.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition is a record kind under RC1-RC12; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

FOLDED IN from B173 (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): More forges: Bitbucket, Gitea/Forgejo and Azure DevOps have no adapter
- **B173. More forges.** Bitbucket, Gitea/Forgejo and Azure DevOps have no adapter. The
  `Forge` interface is five methods; each needs a fake-CLI test like `tests/fakeforge.py`.

Imported from docs/BACKLOG.md:2196.

Move B-semantic-recall and B-mcp-http-transport to P-remote or P-knowledge-hub as the operator says, the fix-test-duration-* and fix-ci-split-slow-tests tasks to a P-test-speed phase, the B-onboard and B-review follow-ups to their owners; B-log-snapshot-knobs joins P-gaps as the first task of B-gap-log-scale, the hub 43 tasks wait for.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. 

STALE NOTE 2026-10-16 (roadmap review): this body names tasks that are already done and counts 22 unphased open tasks; about 60 exist now, including the DX-*, fix-* and LB-* tasks filed since. Recount with `ddflow list task` filtered to no phase at claim time and use that list, not the one above. Fixes and DX tasks keep their own track:dx / track:fix tags and need no phase.

Launching a fleet agent meant pasting the same ~1.5 KB of rules, gate steps, pin recipes, review and test commands, lease and heartbeat rules into every brief (eight times today) and they drifted between launches. The driver text exists (docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md) and the dispatch brief is planned (P-safeguards.dispatch, P-spawn.context); add a command that renders the brief for an item and an agent name from the project's driver, the item's globs, the governing decisions and the current knobs, so one correction reaches every agent. Related: P-safeguards.dispatch, P-agent-parity.launcher. Regression test: the rendered brief contains the item id, the agent flag, the pin recipe and the lease rule.

Filed 2026-10-15 from use (D-file-ddflow-defects). CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-company-workflows): every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

EVIDENCE 2026-10-16: the coordinator wrote about 25 near-identical 2-3 KB agent briefs today (identity, claim, merge main, pins, tests, reviews, forbidden flags, filing rule, report format), roughly 1.5k tokens each, 40k+ in total, plus corrections when a rule changed mid-run. The standard text must come from config/rules (one place), carry the item-specific part only, and include the current operator decisions that bind the files (D-test-economy-r2, D-review-force-with-reason...). Pair with DX-agent-report (the report format) and DX-dispatch-plan.
